title: Code Injection via Invoke-Expression in Generated PowerShell Completion Script
analysis:
Data Flow Analysis:
- Source: Untrusted input enters via the user command-line arguments being typed or autocompleted in PowerShell. In the registered argument completer scriptblock `${__<name>CompleterBlock}`, `$CommandAst.CommandElements` contains the command-line tokens as typed by the user.
- Sanitization/Validation: At lines 58-59, `$Command` is populated by stringifying `$CommandAst.CommandElements` without any escaping or sanitization of command separators or PowerShell subexpressions. At line 84, `$Program,$Arguments = $Command.Split(" ",2)` splits out the arguments. While a special-character filter `__<name>_escapeStringWithSpecialChars` exists at line 46, it is only applied to the completion suggestions (line 243, 267, 275), not to `$Arguments` or `$RequestComp`.
- Sink: At line 129, `$RequestComp` (constructed as `"$Program __complete $Arguments"`) is passed directly to `Invoke-Expression`:
  `Invoke-Expression -OutVariable out "$RequestComp" 2>&1 | Out-Null`
  Because `Invoke-Expression` parses and executes the string as PowerShell code, any PowerShell subexpressions `$(...)` or statement delimiters `;` present in `$Arguments` are immediately evaluated in the current user session before or during autocompletion.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A user types a command with a malicious subexpression or statement separator, or pastes a command line from an untrusted source (or a malicious branch/path argument is typed):
`<program> $(Invoke-Item C:\Windows\System32\calc.exe) <TAB>`
or
`<program> "test"; Start-Process calc.exe; <TAB>`
When the user presses <TAB> to trigger autocompletion, `${__<name>CompleterBlock}` executes, formats `$RequestComp` as `<program> __complete $(Invoke-Item C:\Windows\System32\calc.exe)`, and passes it to `Invoke-Expression`, triggering the execution of `calc.exe`.
vuln_type: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

title: Command Injection via eval in Generated Bash Completion Script (v1)
analysis:
Data Flow Analysis:
- Source: Untrusted input enters via the command-line argument words being completed in Bash. In the bash completion function `__<name>_handle_go_custom_completion`, `_get_comp_words_by_ref "$@"` populates the `words` array representing the command line words typed by the user.
- Sanitization/Validation: At line 89, `args=("${words[@]:1}")` copies all arguments without sanitization. At line 91, `requestComp` is built as `"%[8]s=0 ${words[0]} %[2]s ${args[*]}"` by concatenating the raw arguments.
- Sink: At line 106, `out=$(eval "${requestComp}" 2>/dev/null)` evaluates `requestComp` using the bash `eval` builtin.
  Because `eval` is used to execute the constructed command string, any command substitution `$(...)`, backticks, or shell operators present in the arguments are evaluated by the shell when autocompletion is invoked.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A user types or pastes a command line containing a command substitution or shell metacharacters:
`<program> '$(id)' <TAB>`
or
`<program> ; id ; <TAB>`
When the user presses `<TAB>`, bash autocompletion triggers `__<name>_handle_go_custom_completion`, which executes `eval "${requestComp}"`, running `id`.
vuln_type: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

title: Command Injection via eval in Generated Bash Completion Script (v2)
analysis:
Data Flow Analysis:
- Source: Untrusted input enters via command-line arguments being completed in Bash v2 completions. The `words` array is populated by `_get_comp_words_by_ref` with the command-line tokens.
- Sanitization/Validation: At line 61, `args=("${words[@]:1}")` copies all arguments without sanitization or shell quoting. At line 62, `requestComp="${words[0]} %[2]s ${args[*]}"` joins them into a command string.
- Sink: At line 84, `out=$(eval "${requestComp}" 2>/dev/null)` evaluates `requestComp` using the bash `eval` builtin.
  Passing the string to `eval` causes bash to evaluate command substitutions `$(...)` or backticks embedded in user arguments.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A user types or pastes an argument containing command substitution:
`<program> "$(id)" <TAB>`
When `<TAB>` is pressed, `__<name>_get_completion_results` is called, which evaluates `eval "${requestComp}"`, executing the command `id`.
vuln_type: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

title: Command Injection via eval in Generated Zsh Completion Script
analysis:
Data Flow Analysis:
- Source: Untrusted input enters through user-provided command-line arguments in Zsh. The zsh completion system supplies the command-line tokens via the special `$words` array.
- Sanitization/Validation: At line 140, `requestComp="${words[1]} %[2]s ${words[2,-1]}"` takes the raw argument slice `${words[2,-1]}` and interpolates it into `requestComp` without escaping or quoting shell metacharacters.
- Sink: At line 151, `out=$(eval ${requestComp} 2>/dev/null)` runs `eval` on the command string.
  Because `eval` is used to execute `requestComp`, any shell substitutions like `$(...)` or backticks within `words` are evaluated by zsh.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A user types or pastes an argument containing command substitution into zsh:
`<program> "$(id)" <TAB>`
Upon pressing `<TAB>`, zsh invokes the completion function, which runs `eval ${requestComp}`, executing `id`.
vuln_type: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

title: Command Injection via eval in Generated Fish Completion Script
analysis:
Data Flow Analysis:
- Source: Untrusted input enters via the command-line tokens typed by the user in fish shell, retrieved via `(commandline -opc)`.
- Sanitization/Validation: At lines 48-56, `args (commandline -opc)` are retrieved. While `$lastArg` is escaped using `string escape`, `$args[2..-1]` are not escaped and are concatenated directly into `$requestComp`:
  `set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $args[2..-1] $lastArg"`
- Sink: At line 59, `set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)` runs `eval` on the constructed command string in fish shell.
  Evaluating unescaped argument strings with `eval` allows command substitution in fish shell (e.g. `(...)`) to be executed.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A user types a command with a fish subshell expression:
`<program> (id) <TAB>`
When `<TAB>` is pressed, `__<name>_perform_completion` runs, invoking `eval $requestComp`, which executes `id`.
vuln_type: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
